detailed_rationale:
Meesho Ltd operates a large app-based marketplace connecting sellers and consumers across fashion, electronics and home goods, built around a low-cost, social-commerce-driven model that handled 1.83 billion orders in FY25. Revenue growth remains strong -- TTM revenue of Rs 13,835 crore, up 34% -- reflecting real continued penetration of India's value/budget e-commerce segment, particularly outside the largest metros where Meesho's low-cost logistics and pricing have found genuine traction against Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra.

Profitability, though, remains a long way off: Q1 FY27 posted an operating loss of Rs 225 crore and a net loss of Rs 133 crore, and FY26's full-year net loss was a large Rs 1,358 crore. Sequential trend is only marginally encouraging (operating margin roughly -6% in Q1 FY27 versus -7% in Q4 FY26 -- essentially flat), even as the year-on-year comparison shows margin pressure. ROE (-42%) and ROCE (-35.6%) for the last year are deeply negative, and the stock trades at 19.7x book value despite this -- a rich multiple for a business burning well over a thousand crore a year with only marginal quarter-on-quarter improvement in the loss rate.

Reverse-DCF: 19.7x book value for a company still losing over Rs 1,300 crore a year, in one of the most competitively intense sectors in Indian consumer internet (well-funded rivals, plus increasing encroachment from quick-commerce and D2C brands), requires strong conviction that the path to profitability is close and durable. The sequential margin data (-7% to -6%) shows only marginal movement, not a clear inflection, so I don't have that conviction yet. I side with the quant Sell rather than treat the revenue growth alone as sufficient reason to hold through continued large losses.
recommendation_rationale: Revenue growth (34% TTM) is genuine and reflects real market penetration, but the loss rate has improved only marginally quarter-on-quarter (-7% to -6% operating margin) against a full-year net loss of Rs 1,358 crore, deeply negative ROE/ROCE, and a 19.7x book-value multiple that already prices in a profitability path not yet clearly demonstrated. That combination keeps this at Sell.
summary: Meesho runs one of India's largest value-focused e-commerce marketplaces and continues to grow revenue at a healthy pace, particularly outside major metros. The company remains substantially loss-making, however, and the pace of improvement in that loss has been only marginal quarter to quarter, while the stock trades at a premium to book value that already assumes real progress toward profitability. We rate this a Sell until the path to sustainable profit is more clearly demonstrated.
positive_para: Meesho has built genuine scale and penetration in India's value e-commerce segment (1.83 billion orders in FY25) with a distinctive low-cost, social-commerce model, and TTM revenue growth of 34% shows the demand pull is real, not manufactured. The company carries very little debt, giving it flexibility to keep investing in the path to profitability without near-term financing pressure.
negative_para: The business is still deeply loss-making -- a Rs 1,358 crore net loss in FY26 and continued losses this quarter -- with ROE of -42% and ROCE of -35.6%, and the sequential improvement in operating margin (-7% to -6%) has been only marginal rather than a clear inflection. At 19.7x book value, the market is already crediting Meesho with meaningful progress toward profitability in an intensely competitive e-commerce market that this quarter's numbers do not yet clearly support.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A 19.7x book-value multiple for a business still losing well over a thousand crore rupees a year requires confidence that profitability is close and durable; the sequential margin data shows only marginal improvement, not a clear inflection, so that confidence is not yet warranted. Given ROE remains deeply negative, this does not qualify for the exceptional/low-dilution growth tier despite the strong revenue trajectory.
